name: spaced-practice-scheduler
description: Design a spaced retrieval schedule for any topic list and timeline. Use when planning units, term sequences, or revision programmes.
evidence_sources: Ebbinghaus (1885/1913) — The forgetting curve: exponential decay of memory without review
Cepeda et al. (2006) — Quantitative synthesis of 317 experiments in 184 articles on distributed practice in verbal recall: effective spacing depends on the retention interval
Kornell & Bjork (2008) — Spacing and interleaving effects on learning
Carpenter et al. (2012) — Using spacing to enhance diverse forms of learning
Dunlosky et al. (2013) — Distributed practice rated high-utility learning strategy

required.description: List of topics or concepts to be spaced across the schedule
Available teaching period (e.g. '6-week half-term' or 'Term 2: Jan 15 – Mar 28')
Number of lessons per week for this subject

optional.description: Date of summative assessment, if known — affects final spacing intervals
Teacher's estimate of relative difficulty for each topic (high/medium/low)
From context engine: mandated teaching order or prerequisite dependencies
From context engine: class-level retention data from prior assessments

fields.description: Week-by-week schedule showing new teaching and spaced review slots
Explanation of why topics are spaced at these intervals
Brief retrieval activities for each review slot
How to implement the schedule and adjust based on student response
